name: greek-alphabet

description.en: The 24 letters of the Greek alphabet in 24 cards, studied in both directions. The front shows a letter in upper and lower case (Α α), the back its name in English and Swedish (alpha, alfa). Names and characters from Wikidata, checked against the Unicode Character Database, Svenska Akademiens ordlista, the SALDO lexicon and Nationalencyklopedin.
description.sv: Det grekiska alfabetets 24 bokstäver på 24 kort, som övas åt båda hållen. Framsidan visar en bokstav som versal och gemen (Α α), baksidan dess namn på engelska och svenska (alpha, alfa). Namnen och tecknen kommer från Wikidata och har kontrollerats mot Unicodes teckendatabas, Svenska Akademiens ordlista, lexikonet SALDO och Nationalencyklopedin.

(SALDO also gives second base forms for four of the senses: thäta in theta..1, iota in jota..2, ro in rho..1 and phi in fi..1; these variants are not used on the cards.)

ne.usedFor: Check of the Swedish names zeta, theta, kappa, my, ny, xi, omikron, rho, tau, ypsilon, fi, chi and psi (each an NE headword defined as a letter of the Greek alphabet) and of jota (a cross-reference to NE's entry iota). NE's entry for eta could not be found under /eta.

method: Who did the work: Anton Wiklund compiled this deck with the help of AI agents (Claude, by Anthropic), which did the research, drafting and cross-checking at his direction. The cards were checked by machine (live Wikidata and the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators) and in independent review rounds by further Claude agents, each logged under Quality control with its findings and how they were resolved. Anton Wiklund reviews every deck in full before it is released.

Selection: the Wikidata Query Service (https://query.wikidata.org/sparql) was asked for every value of has part(s) (P527) of Greek alphabet (Q8216), with English and Swedish labels, classes and Unicode characters (P487) (query 1). It returned exactly 24 items, one per letter of the standard 24-letter alphabet, and no others.

Labels and aliases: a second SPARQL query for the English, Swedish and mul labels and aliases (query 2) returned no values because of how it combined OPTIONAL and GROUP_CONCAT, so the same data was read from the Wikidata API instead (query 3, wbgetentities for the 24 items with labels, aliases and claims in en, sv and mul) and printed with a small Python script that, for each of the 24 items in alphabet order, printed its labels and aliases per language and the values of P487 (Unicode character), P31, P279 and P361, without filtering. The Swedish labels are the Swedish names on the cards. The English labels of 18 items are the letters themselves (for example "Α/α"), so the English name was taken from the label or alias that spells the name: an exact lower-case label or alias for 18 letters (alpha, beta, delta, epsilon, zeta, eta, theta, iota, kappa, lambda, mu, nu, omicron, pi, sigma, phi, psi, omega); for gamma, rho, tau and upsilon Wikidata gives the name only capitalised ("Gamma", "Rho", "Tau", "Upsilon"), for xi only in phrases such as "xi (Greek letter)" and for chi as "chi (Greek)"; these six are written in lower case, as the other names are.

Card fronts: each front is the upper-case letter, a space and the lower-case letter, written with the Greek code points U+0391–U+03A9 and U+03B1–U+03C9 (never the look-alike Latin letters, the micro sign U+00B5 or the ohm sign U+2126). The characters come from Wikidata: the Unicode character (P487) values of each item, and for the letters without them (capital alpha, iota, nu, xi, omicron) the single-character English aliases Α, Ι/ι, Ν/ν, Ξ/ξ and Ο/ο, which are the same Greek code points. They were compared with the Unicode Character Database's UnicodeData.txt (version 18.0.0, command 4): every front character is the GREEK CAPITAL LETTER or GREEK SMALL LETTER of the card's name. The builder's checks confirm every front character against Wikidata (step 7).

English names were cross-checked against the Unicode character names: all 24 agree except that Unicode names λ GREEK SMALL LETTER LAMDA; its Unicode 1.0 name field gives GREEK SMALL LETTER LAMBDA, and Wikidata gives both lambda and lamda as aliases. The card says lambda, the usual English spelling.

Swedish names were checked against four sources. (a) Svenska Akademiens ordlista (SAOL) and Svensk ordbok (SO) through the search API behind svenska.se (commands 5 and 6, https://svenska.se/api/search/saol?q=<word> and …/so?q=<word>, first ranked and then with exactMatch=true): SAOL has 11 of the names as headwords defined as a Greek letter (alfa, beta, gamma, delta, epsilon, jota, lambda, pi, sigma, ypsilon, omega), SO 5 of them (alfa, beta, gamma, delta, omega); neither has the other 13 (SAOL and SO have kappa only as the garment and ny only as the adjective and the moon phase) nor the alternative spellings khi, teta, ksi or phi. (b) SALDO, Språkbanken's lexicon of Swedish, through the Karp API (command 7, equals|baseform|<word>): all 24 Wikidata Swedish names are base forms of a sense with primary descriptor bokstav (letter) and secondary descriptor grekiska (Greek); khi, teta and ksi are not SALDO base forms; four of the senses have a second base form, which the cards do not use: thäta (theta..1), iota (jota..2), ro (rho..1) and phi (fi..1). (c) The table in Swedish Wikipedia's article Grekiska alfabetet (command 8, revision 59450821) lists the same 24 Swedish names. (d) In quality-control round 2, Nationalencyklopedin's entries (command 14, https://www.ne.se/uppslagsverk/encyklopedi/lång/<word>) confirmed zeta, theta, kappa, my, ny, xi, omikron, rho, tau, ypsilon, fi, chi and psi as headwords defined as Greek letters, and jota as a cross-reference to iota; NE also has khi ("annan translitterering" of chi) and phi ("se fi"). Every Swedish name on the cards is thus the Wikidata Swedish label and confirmed by SALDO and, where they have the word, by SAOL and NE.

Machine checks: every card has a check that its Swedish name is the Wikidata Swedish label of its item; 18 cards also check the English name as a Wikidata English label or alias; every front character is checked against Wikidata, as a Unicode character (P487) value (20 cards) or, for capital alpha, iota, nu, xi and omicron, as an English label or alias. The builder runs these against live Wikidata on every check and build.

Notes: only the sigma card has a note. It gives the word-final form ς, taken from Wikidata: Q14413's Unicode character (P487) value "ς" has the qualifier applies to part (P518) final form (Q5449465, described as "conditional form of a grapheme at the end of a word"); verified with Unicode (U+03C2 GREEK SMALL LETTER FINAL SIGMA) and Swedish Wikipedia's table entry "ς (avslutande sigma)". Variant Swedish spellings (thäta for theta, iota for jota, ro for rho, phi for fi, khi for chi) are not given in notes: Wikidata, the deck's only content source, does not have them as Swedish names; only verification sources (SALDO, NE) do, and under the licence policy a verification source contributes nothing to the cards. The note text is the authoring agent's own wording.

Exclusions: archaic letters (digamma, koppa, sampi, san, heta) and variant glyphs (ϐ, ϑ, ϰ, ϖ, ϱ, ϕ, ϒ, ϵ) are left out; letter order, numeric values, pronunciation and transliteration are not asked, because they vary between ancient and modern Greek and between transliteration schemes.
selection: The deck has exactly the 24 letters of the standard (Ionic, classical and modern) Greek alphabet, as listed by Wikidata's has part(s) statements on Greek alphabet (Q8216): one card per letter, front the upper- and lower-case letter, back the letter's English and Swedish names. The word-final form of sigma (ς) is not a letter of its own and is given in the sigma card's note. Left out: archaic letters that dropped out of the alphabet (digamma, koppa, sampi, san, heta), variant glyphs used in mathematics (ϑ, ϕ, ϖ and others), alternative Swedish spellings that are not Wikidata Swedish labels or aliases (teta and ksi, which no source checked has; thäta, iota, ro, phi and khi, which SALDO or Nationalencyklopedin list as variants but which the content source does not give), and anything that differs between ancient and modern Greek, such as pronunciation, transliteration and numeric values.

queries.purpose: Query 1: the letters of the Greek alphabet (Q8216 has part(s)), their English and Swedish labels, classes and Unicode characters.
Query 2: English, Swedish and mul labels and aliases of the letters. It returned rows without values and was replaced by query 3.
Query 3: labels, aliases and statements of the 24 letter items.
Command 4: the Unicode character names of the Greek capital and small letters U+0391–U+03A9 and U+03B1–U+03C9 (UCD version from ReadMe.txt: 18.0.0).

curl -s -A "solid-memo deck research (https://github.com/antwika/solid-memo)" -o UnicodeData.txt https://www.unicode.org/Public/UCD/latest/ucd/UnicodeData.txt

grep -E "^03(9[1-9A-F]|A[0-9]|A[3-9]|B[1-9A-F]|C[0-9])" UnicodeData.txt

queries.purpose: Command 5: SAOL search for each candidate Swedish name, ranked (size=10) and exact (size=30&exactMatch=true); headwords equal to the word and their definitions were printed. Words: alfa alpha beta gamma delta epsilon zeta eta theta teta jota iota kappa lambda lamda my ny xi ksi omikron omicron pi rho rå ro sigma tau ypsilon upsilon fi phi khi chi psi omega (the exact pass for zeta eta theta teta kappa my ny xi ksi omikron rho tau fi khi chi psi epsilon sigma ypsilon lambda jota).
Command 6: the same searches in Svensk ordbok, with the same word lists.

Command 7: SALDO senses whose base form is each candidate Swedish name (alfa beta gamma delta epsilon zeta eta theta teta jota kappa lambda my ny xi ksi omikron pi rho sigma tau ypsilon fi phi khi chi psi omega), with their primary and secondary descriptors.

Command 8: the wikitext of Swedish Wikipedia's Grekiska alfabetet, its table of letters and names. The revision read was 59450821 (2026-07-07), identified in round 3 with command 13; its raw text (oldid=59450821) is byte-identical to the text read with this command.

queries.purpose: Licence of Wikidata (fetched in round 3; the quote was also checked when the deck was drafted).
Licence of Wikipedia text (Wikimedia Terms of Use, section 7; fetched in round 3).
Rights statement of svenska.se (SAOL and SO; page footer; fetched in round 3).
Command 9 (round 3): the Unicode character (P487) statements of omega and sigma with their qualifiers, and the label of Q5449465 (final form).
Command 10 (round 3): labels and aliases (en, sv, mul) of alpha, iota, nu, xi, omicron, phi and chi, printed with each single-character alias and its code point.
Command 11 (round 3): the SALDO senses with base form jota.
Command 12 (round 3): where the Unicode terms of use now live.
Command 13 (round 3): the current revision id of Grekiska alfabetet, and its raw text for comparison with command 8's.

Command 14 (round 2): Nationalencyklopedin's entries for the candidate Swedish names, text around the word "bokstav" printed. Words: chi khi fi phi my ny xi theta rho omikron ypsilon tau zeta eta psi kappa jota.
Licence of Nationalencyklopedin (the page's link "Upphovsrätt").

Command 15 (round 4): command 7's query re-run for the 24 Swedish names on the cards (alfa beta gamma delta epsilon zeta eta theta jota kappa lambda my ny xi omikron pi rho sigma tau ypsilon fi chi psi omega), printing for each sense with primary bokstav..1 its senseID, all base forms and secondary descriptors.

licensing: The deck is CC0 1.0. Its only content source is Wikidata, whose structured data is CC0: the selection of the 24 letters, their Swedish labels, English names, characters and the word-final form of sigma come from it. The Unicode Character Database (Unicode License v3, a permissive licence that asks for its notice to accompany copies of the data files), Svenska Akademiens ordlista and Svensk ordbok (© Svenska Akademien), SALDO (CC BY 4.0 according to Språkbanken's metadata, with a ShareAlike phrase in its description), Nationalencyklopedin (all rights reserved; quoting allowed only non-commercially) and Swedish Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0) were used for verification only: they confirmed facts Wikidata gave (letter names and code points, which as facts are not copyrightable), and no text, list, selection or additional fact was taken from them. Variant spellings that only these sources give (thäta, iota, ro, phi, khi) were deliberately left off the cards for this reason. The note is the authoring agent's own wording. So no source's licence imposes conditions on the deck, and it can be CC0 like the rest of the library.

rounds.scope: All 24 cards: selection, front characters, English and Swedish names, notes; the builder's Wikidata checks; the app's SHACL and DCAT-AP validators.
rounds.summary: Wikidata (query 1) lists exactly the 24 letters. Every front's characters are the Greek letters of the card's name in UnicodeData.txt. Every English name agrees with Wikidata and the Unicode character names (lambda: see below). Every Swedish name is the Wikidata Swedish label and a SALDO base form for a Greek letter; 11 are also SAOL headwords. The builder's checks cover all 24 Swedish labels, 18 English names and 20 fronts' characters (P487), and pass. Discrepancies and gaps are listed below.

findings.card: gamma, rho, tau, upsilon, xi, chi
findings.issue: Wikidata has no exact lower-case English label or alias for these six letters: it gives "Gamma", "Rho", "Tau", "Upsilon" capitalised, xi only as "xi (Greek letter)" and similar phrases, and chi as "chi (Greek)". An English label check would fail.
findings.resolution: The names are written in lower case like the other 18; no English label check is added for these cards (no check was dropped because Wikidata disagrees on the name). The Unicode character names (GAMMA, RHO, TAU, UPSILON, XI, CHI) confirm them.

findings.issue: Unicode names the character GREEK CAPITAL/SMALL LETTER LAMDA, not LAMBDA; Wikidata has the aliases lambda and lamda.
findings.resolution: Kept lambda, the usual English spelling: Unicode's own Unicode 1.0 name field for U+039B and U+03BB is GREEK CAPITAL LETTER LAMBDA and GREEK SMALL LETTER LAMBDA, and Wikidata has the alias lambda (checked).

findings.issue: The brief suggested the Swedish spelling khi or chi. SAOL and SO have neither as a headword. (Corrected in round 2: Nationalencyklopedin, read then, has chi as the headword and khi as "annan translitterering".)
findings.resolution: Chose chi: it is the Wikidata Swedish label, the SALDO base form for the Greek letter (khi is not in SALDO) and the name in Swedish Wikipedia's table.

findings.issue: Possible Swedish alternatives teta and ksi.
findings.resolution: Neither is in SAOL, SO or SALDO; theta and xi are the Wikidata Swedish labels, SALDO base forms and the names in Swedish Wikipedia's table. Kept theta and xi.

findings.card: zeta, eta, theta, kappa, mu, nu, xi, omicron, rho, tau, phi, chi, psi
findings.issue: SAOL has no headword for these 13 Swedish letter names (kappa only as the garment, ny only as the adjective and the moon phase), so the brief's verification against SAOL is not possible for them; Nationalencyklopedin's article could not be read (the page returned an error). (Round 2: NE could be read then and confirms all of these except eta, whose entry was not found under /eta; see the cards' evidence.)
findings.resolution: Verified with SALDO, where each is the base form of a sense described as a Greek letter, and with Swedish Wikipedia's table.

findings.issue: Wikidata's Unicode character (P487) is missing for iota, nu, xi and omicron, and gives only the lower-case α for alpha.
findings.resolution: No P487 check for the missing values; the fronts were checked against UnicodeData.txt. (Round 3 added Wikidata checks of these characters as English aliases.)

findings.issue: Wikidata's P487 for mu includes the micro sign µ (U+00B5). For omega, P487 has a third value that is stored as U+03A9 (Wikibase normalises strings to NFC, which maps the ohm sign U+2126 to U+03A9) and is marked as the ohm sign only by its qualifier Unicode hex codepoint (P4213) = 2126. (Wording corrected in round 3; it first said the ohm sign itself was stored.)
findings.resolution: The fronts use the Greek code points U+039C/U+03BC and U+03A9/U+03C9, verified with a script; the checks test these code points.

findings.issue: SALDO gives phi as a second base form of the Swedish sense fi..1, and Swedish Wikipedia's prose uses Phi.
findings.resolution: Kept fi (Wikidata Swedish label, first SALDO base form, Swedish Wikipedia's table) and gave phi in a note. (Round 3 removed the note: only verification sources give phi as a Swedish spelling.)

findings.issue: Wikidata also has the English aliases mi and ni (modern Greek pronunciations).
findings.resolution: Used mu and nu, the names in Unicode and the established English spellings.

rounds.scope: All 24 cards: re-verified against live Wikidata, UnicodeData.txt, SAOL, SALDO and Swedish Wikipedia; the builder's Wikidata checks.
rounds.summary: No factual errors in the 24 cards. Three optional suggestions: soften the phi note, cite Swedish Wikipedia's table entry for final sigma, and adjust the description's "Names from Wikidata".

findings.issue: The note "Also spelled phi in Swedish." rests on thin support (SALDO only; SAOL and SO lack phi; Swedish Wikipedia uses Phi only in running prose).
findings.resolution: Confirmed. The note was removed altogether (see round 3, finding 1: the spelling comes only from verification sources).

findings.issue: The Swedish Wikipedia sentence cited for the final-sigma note is about medieval minuscule, not the present-day rule; the table entry "ς (avslutande sigma)" supports it more directly.
findings.resolution: Confirmed in the wikitext (revision 59450821): the table row after Σ σ reads "ς | (avslutande sigma)". The evidence now cites that entry; the note's fact itself is now traced to Wikidata's P518 final-form qualifier (round 3, finding 3).

findings.issue: The description says "Names from Wikidata", but for gamma, rho, tau, upsilon, xi and chi Wikidata has no exact lower-case English name; the suggestion was "Names from Wikidata and the Unicode Character Database".
findings.resolution: Not adopted as worded: the Unicode Character Database is a verification source and cannot be named as a source of the names. The six names are in Wikidata ("Gamma", "Rho", "Tau", "Upsilon", "xi (Greek letter)", "chi (Greek)"); writing them in lower case is an editorial normalisation documented in method step 3 and round 0. The description now says "Names and characters from Wikidata" and adds Nationalencyklopedin to the checks (round 2).

rounds.reviewer: Claude (AI) — independent language and translation reviewer
rounds.scope: All 24 cards: front code points, language tags, Swedish names against SAOL, SO, SALDO and Nationalencyklopedin, English and Swedish notes and description; the builder's Wikidata checks.
rounds.summary: No language errors. One warning (the chi card should note the variant khi, and the dossier wrongly said no checked source has khi) and four suggestions (add NE as a verification source, reword the phi and sigma English notes, use "har kontrollerats" in the Swedish description).

findings.issue: Nationalencyklopedin has khi as another rendering of chi ("khi, annan translitterering av den grekiska bokstaven chi"); the card gives no hint of it, unlike the phi card, and the selection text says no checked dictionary has khi.
findings.resolution: Confirmed NE's entries (command 14). The note is not added: Wikidata, the only content source, has no Swedish khi (only the English alias "khi (Greek)"), and under the licence policy a fact found only in a verification source (NE, all rights reserved) may not be added to the cards. For consistency the phi note was removed as well (round 3), so no card gives a variant spelling. The selection text and round 0 were corrected so they no longer say that no checked source has khi, and NE's khi entry is cited in the chi card's evidence.

findings.issue: Nationalencyklopedin, which round 0 could not read, can now be read and confirms nearly all the Swedish names that rest only on SALDO and Swedish Wikipedia.
findings.resolution: Re-fetched NE myself (command 14): it confirms zeta, theta, kappa, my, ny, xi, omikron, rho, tau, ypsilon, fi, chi and psi as headwords defined as Greek letters, and jota as a cross-reference to iota; /eta gave no Greek-letter entry. Added NE as a verification source (all rights reserved; https://www.ne.se/info/upphovsratt/) with its quote on each of these 14 cards, updated method step 6, the description and round 0.

findings.issue: The English note "Also spelled phi in Swedish." next to the English back "phi" is confusing.
findings.resolution: The note no longer exists (removed in round 3, finding 1).

findings.issue: "the lower case is written ς" uses "lower case" awkwardly as a noun.
findings.resolution: English note changed to "At the end of a word, lower-case sigma is written ς."; the Swedish note is unchanged.

findings.issue: Swedish description: "är kontrollerade mot" reads as stative; "har kontrollerats mot" fits a process carried out.
findings.resolution: Changed to "Namnen och tecknen kommer från Wikidata och har kontrollerats mot …, lexikonet SALDO och Nationalencyklopedin." (Nationalencyklopedin also added to the English description).

rounds.reviewer: Claude (AI) — independent licensing, attribution and documentation reviewer
rounds.scope: All 24 cards and every source: licences and their evidence, the licence policy, attribution, evidence "says" against the live sources, queries and reproducibility.
rounds.summary: One error (the phi note's fact came only from a verification source), three warnings (omega P487 wording, sigma note traced only to verification sources, front characters without P487 not machine-checked) and four suggestions (Unicode licence wording, iota SALDO base forms, SALDO version, reproducibility gaps). All were confirmed against the live sources and fixed.

findings.issue: The note "Also spelled phi in Swedish." states a fact only SALDO (a verification source) gives; Wikidata has no Swedish phi, contrary to the licence policy and the licensing paragraph.
findings.resolution: Confirmed: Q10029 has Swedish label "fi" and no Swedish aliases; "phi" is an English alias. Removed the note so the deck stays CC0 and Wikidata-sourced; method step 8 and the licensing paragraph now explain why variant spellings (phi, khi, iota) are not given. No iota note is added for the same reason.

findings.issue: The evidence says P487 holds the ohm sign U+2126; the stored value is U+03A9 with qualifier P4213 = 2126.
findings.resolution: Confirmed with wbgetclaims (command 9). The omega Wikidata evidence and the round 0 finding "mu, omega" now state what is stored.

findings.issue: The note's "end of a word" fact is supported only by verification sources; Wikidata's P518 final-form qualifier supports it but is not cited.
findings.resolution: Confirmed (command 9): ς has P518 = Q5449465 "final form", "conditional form of a grapheme at the end of a word". The sigma Wikidata evidence, Wikidata's usedFor and method step 8 now cite it.

findings.issue: usedFor and method step 4 say the front characters come from P487, but iota, nu, xi and omicron have no P487 and alpha only α; their characters come from labels and aliases and are not machine-checked.
findings.resolution: Confirmed (command 10): the English aliases are the Greek code points. usedFor and method steps 4 and 7 now say so, the evidence lists the aliases, and nine checks were added (Q9887 Α; Q14399 Ι, ι; Q14402 Ν, ν; Q14406 Ξ, ξ; Q14408 Ο, ο), so every front character is checked against Wikidata.

findings.issue: The Unicode Character Database's licence is shown as "Unknown" though it is the Unicode License v3; terms_of_use.html now redirects to copyright.html.
findings.resolution: Confirmed the redirect (command 12). licenseEvidence now begins with "Licence: Unicode License v3 (SPDX Unicode-3.0), recorded as \"unknown\" only because the builder has no licence id for it" and cites copyright.html. Adding Unicode-3.0 to the builder's licences is left to the maintainer (the builder is outside this deck's scope).

findings.issue: The SALDO evidence gives base form "jota" only; jota..2 has base forms "iota" and "jota".
findings.resolution: Confirmed (command 11). Evidence corrected. Jota is kept because it is the Wikidata Swedish label, the SAOL headword ("en grekisk bokstav"), Swedish Wikipedia's table name and an NE cross-reference; iota is not given in a note because Wikidata has no Swedish iota.

findings.issue: The SALDO title cites "version 2", but the Karp API serves the daily development version.
findings.resolution: Confirmed on https://sprakbanken.se/en/resources/saldo ("The web services are updated daily with the latest development version of SALDO"). Retitled "SALDO (Swedish Associative Thesaurus), development version through Språkbanken's Karp API (v7), queried 2026-10-04".

findings.issue: Reproducibility gaps: no Swedish Wikipedia revision id; licence-page fetches for Wikidata, the Wikimedia Terms of Use and svenska.se not in the queries; the printing script not described; method step 1 mentions review rounds not yet recorded.
findings.resolution: (a) Revision 59450821 (2026-07-07) identified (command 13); its raw text is byte-identical to what command 8 read, and the source URL and title now pin it. (b) The licence-page fetches are now listed in the queries (re-fetched today; the quotes match). (c) Method step 3 now describes what the script printed (no filtering). (d) The three review rounds are recorded here, and step 1 names them.

rounds.lens: Final re-check (loop 1): the 17 changed cards plus every third card (alpha, delta, eta, kappa, nu, pi, tau, chi, among others), checked for facts and language; metadata, licence decision, documentation and the accuracy of the qualityControl log
rounds.scope: 20 cards (the 17 changed in rounds 1–3 plus every third card), metadata, licence decision, documentation and the qualityControl log; the builder's Wikidata checks and the SHACL and DCAT-AP validators.
rounds.summary: No card text was wrong. Two warnings (the SALDO evidence for theta and rho left out a second base form) and one suggestion (the dossier's lists of SALDO variants missed the same two). All three were confirmed by re-running the SALDO query for all 24 names (command 15), which showed that only theta..1, jota..2, rho..1 and fi..1 have more than one base form, and were fixed in the documentation; no card text changed.

findings.issue: The SALDO evidence gives base form "theta" only; theta..1 has base forms "theta" and "thäta".
findings.resolution: Confirmed (command 15: theta..1, lemgrams theta..nn.1 and thäta..nn.1, baseform ["theta", "thäta"]). Evidence corrected. Thäta is not put on the card: Wikidata, the only content source, has no Swedish thäta.

findings.issue: The SALDO evidence gives base form "rho" only; rho..1 has base forms "rho" and "ro".
findings.resolution: Confirmed (command 15: rho..1, lemgrams rho..nn.1 and ro..nn.3, baseform ["rho", "ro"]). Evidence corrected. Ro is not put on the card, for the same reason as thäta.

findings.issue: The SALDO usedFor, method steps 6 and 8, the selection text and the licensing paragraph name only phi and iota (with khi) as variant spellings, leaving out SALDO's thäta and ro.
findings.resolution: Confirmed that the four senses with a second base form are theta..1 (thäta), jota..2 (iota), rho..1 (ro) and fi..1 (phi), and no others among the 24 (command 15). All five places now list thäta, iota, ro, phi and khi (the last from NE).
